chunks: 4587 - And it is narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, who said:
A man asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام:

About a man who marries a woman in mutʿah and stipulates with her that he will not seek her child; then afterward she brings a child, and he denies the child. So he spoke sternly regarding that and said, “He denies it? And how can he deny it?” magnifying the seriousness of that. The man said: “Then if he suspects her?” He said: “It is not proper for you to marry except a trustworthy woman. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:
“The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatress or a polytheist, and the fornicatress—none marries her except a fornicator or a polytheist; and that has been forbidden to the believers.”

key_terms.بِمَأْمُونَةٍ: a trustworthy woman, one relied upon in chastity and integrity
key_terms.فَيُنْكِرُ: he denies, meaning he rejects attribution of the child
key_terms.وَلَدَهَا: her child, referring here to offspring attributed through the marriage

ai.seo_question: Can a man deny a child born from a mutʿah marriage if he had stipulated that he did not want children?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses rulings and moral seriousness related to mutʿah, paternity, and suspicion between spouses. Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام strongly condemns denying a child born from such a union and instructs that one should marry only a trustworthy woman, citing a Qur'anic verse about illicit sexual conduct. The report combines family law with ethical caution and Qur'anic guidance.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4587 - It is narrated from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazee who said:

A man asked Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha (as) about a man who marries a woman in Mutah (temporary marriage) and stipulates with her that he will not seek a child from her. However, she later gives birth to a child, and the man denies the child.
Al-Ridha (as) expressed strong disapproval of this and said:
"He denies it? How can he deny it?" - emphasizing the gravity of such an act.
The man then asked: "What if he suspects her (of wrongdoing)?"
Imam Al-Ridha (as) replied: "You should not marry except a trustworthy woman. Verily, Allah (swt), the Exalted, said:

'The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatress or a polytheist, and the fornicatress does not marry except a fornicator or a polytheist, and this has been forbidden for the believers.'" (Surah Al-Nur, 24:3)
